shots.title: Resolve the trunk to the remote-tracking ref with a documented fallback to the local ref (#687)

hazards.description: The first cut broke the shell-injection guard. Replacing the candidate list with [resolved.ref, 'main', 'master', 'HEAD'] meant an EXPLICIT unsafe ref no longer short-circuited to an empty set — it was skipped by SAFE_REF_RE and then silently fell through to scanning main. The existing 'refuses unsafe refs' test caught it. Explicit refs must be honoured alone, never widened to defaults.

shots.notes: resolveTrunkRef prefers the local trunk's configured upstream (main@{upstream}), then the remote's recorded default branch (refs/remotes/origin/HEAD), then the local branch, then HEAD, reporting which source won and how far the local trunk is behind. findShippedSprintsOnMain scans through it. Scored as a miss: the security regression shipped into the working tree and was caught by an existing test, not by design.

shots.title: Warn when the local and remote-tracking trunk diverge, since that is the condition that makes the check meaningless (#687)
shots.notes: slope roadmap validate now prints which ref it scanned and how far the local trunk is behind, but only when they have actually diverged — a quiet no-op in the main checkout, informative in a worktree. Divergence is the condition that makes shipped-commit detection meaningless, so it belongs next to the result, not in a separate command.

shots.title: Cover the four shipped-commit consumers with worktree fixtures so status, retro, validate and the guard agree (#687)

hazards.description: mkdtempSync appends a random suffix to its argument, so mkdtempSync(join(root,'origin')) does not create 'origin' — it creates 'originAbC123'. Every git command then ran in a non-existent cwd and surfaced as `spawnSync cmd.exe ENOENT`, which reads like a missing git rather than a missing directory. Use mkdirSync for a known path.

shots.notes: tests/core/analyzers/trunk-ref.test.ts builds a real origin, a clone whose local main is deliberately left behind, and a worktree off that clone. Asserts the merged sprint is found from both the clone and the worktree, and that the two agree — the four consumers (roadmap validate, slope status, slope retro, post-hole-enforcement) all read one helper, so agreement at the helper is agreement everywhere.

bunker_locations: src/core/analyzers/git.ts findShippedSprintsOnMain: an explicit ref argument must be scanned alone. Appending the default candidates after it turns an unsafe-ref rejection into a silent scan of a different branch.
Node's mkdtempSync appends a random suffix; it never creates the exact path passed to it. In git fixtures the resulting ENOENT surfaces as a spawn failure and reads like a missing binary.
notes: Fixes #687. Blast radius was four times what the issue described: findShippedSprintsOnMain resolved ['main','master','HEAD'] — all local refs — and four call sites consume it, so roadmap validate, slope status, slope retro and the post-hole-enforcement guard all mis-reported together in a worktree. Since worktrees are the recommended way to run parallel sprints here, the check was always-on-and-wrong in exactly the workflow SLOPE encourages. Full suite green (4320 passed).
